    - `DGS1MO`, `DGS3MO`, `DGS6MO`, `DGS1`, `SOFR`, and `DFF`.
    
    Hard rules:
    
    - `HistoricalScope` admits a registered session before any path is formed. No wildcard year discovery and no 2026 path before escrow authorization.
    - Raw tape timestamps remain naive ET/frame B until the registry-backed `SessionClock` converts them exactly once to UTC/frame A. Test EST, EDT, early closes, and one-hour/double-shift mutants.
    - Inventory every physical schema and size/unit era. Refuse unseen layouts. Include 2025-10-31, 2025-11-03, and 2025-11-04 in the pilot to straddle the stock size/attached-NBBO break.
    - Group equal timestamps across every shard before aggregation. Authenticate source sequence only within its source; otherwise use commutative summaries and mark order ambiguous. File and shard order cannot affect tensors.
    - Classify stock trades only with their attached strictly-prior NBBO. Missing/equal/future attached timestamps become distinct unresolved states.
    - Use stock spot strictly before each option event. Never use the final quote of a second for an earlier event.
    - Reconstruct sweeps causally; vendor whole-sweep totals are unavailable until the terminal member.
    - Preserve missing, stale, invalid, one-sided, locked, crossed, unknown-condition, venue, and unit-era states.
    - Ban `price_lead_1` and every future-return equivalent statically.
    - OI is usable only when its physical timestamp is before the session open; otherwise carry the previous valid observation. Publish unsigned exposure and both dealer-sign scenarios.
    - The local FRED files are current-vintage and cannot be used scientifically. Acquire lawful ALFRED/as-of vintages or mask the rate family.
    - Do not run one Black–Scholes inverter for both products. RUTW quote IV requires validated European/cash-settlement inputs; IWM raw quote IV requires a validated American/dividend/exercise model. Until then mark IWM raw bid/ask IV as `IV_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED` and retain vendor AllGreeks IV/error fields.
    - RUTW is contextual state only. IWM remains the only action clock, executable price, and P&L authority; no RUT/RTY payload enters science.
    
    ### State publications
    
    Publish per-session Parquet authority plus a manifest-keyed derived mmap cache:
    
    - `fast_core`: 144 channels—stock 48, IWM option prints 48, RUTW option prints 32, cross-stream mechanisms 16.
    - `fast_quotes`: IWM option quotes 48 and RUTW option quotes 32.
    - `slow`: 144 channels—surface/higher Greeks 64, session path/realized volatility 32, OI/PIT rates/forward state 48.
    - `action_query`: at most 16 channels per side containing explicit side/direction and causal constituent/event geometry only.
    - Packed two-bit numeric availability `{VALID, STALE, INVALID, MISSING}`; one-sided/locked/crossed/condition/unit states remain explicit capped feature channels.
    - Windows are half-open: fast input is the previous 240 seconds, and slow input is session-to-date completed minutes. No cutoff-minute or later value is visible.
    
    The frozen-calendar uncompressed budget is 20.994 GiB: 23,373,000 seconds, 389,550 minutes, nine early closes, and all masks/query state. Hard publication cap is 30 GiB.
    
    Compile this exact 20-session pilot first:
    
    ```text
    2022-01-03, 2022-01-04, 2022-11-01,
    2023-06-05, 2023-11-24,
    2024-06-03, 2024-07-17, 2024-07-18, 2024-07-19,
    2024-07-31, 2024-08-01, 2024-11-29,
    2025-04-07, 2025-10-31, 2025-11-03, 2025-11-04,
    2025-12-18, 2025-12-24, 2025-12-30, 2025-12-31
    ```
    
    Pilot budgets: core ≤20 minutes, quotes ≤15 minutes, RSS ≤16 GiB, workers ≤8. Full inventory ≤2 hours, each full compiler ≤6 hours. Complete the full raw-quote pass even if summary features are null before declaring the available information set exhausted. A family consuming over 20% of recurring pipeline time is killed after its measured one-time test.
    
    ### Mechanisms
    
    Implement only budgeted, observable mechanisms:
    
    - Stock pressure at fast/slow EWMs, spread/depth instability, refill/defense, aggression, unresolved flow, arrival runs, and effort-versus-price response.
    - IWM/RUTW option premium and Greek flow, expiry/moneyness structure, condition/venue/sweep state, and stock response—without assuming informed direction or dealer sign.
    - Defense-to-handoff state: high effort with falling resistance, response elasticity, residual continuation/reversal, cross-venue recruitment, and post-event residual sink.
    - A 16-channel trailing cross-impact block. Let `q_t` be unexpected delta/vega/skew/term flow after an EWM-60 expectation. Using only `s < t` over 240 seconds:
    
    ```text
    B_t = (X'WX + λI)^−1 X'WY
    λ   = 1e−3 * trace(X'WX) / 4
    ```
    
    Emit projected response, residual, alignment, trailing R², singular-value ratios, recruitment, refill, and sink state.
    
    The prior-session analog diagnostic was null on 91,863 aggregate rows. Permit exactly one preregistered rich-state attempt using masked cosine, cutoff ±5 bars, `k=128`, and at most four neighbors per prior session. Kill it if its F1–F5 gate fails. BOCPD, committor learning, and learned transition candidates remain conditional pivots only.
    
    ### Controls and primary model
    
    Use one fixed XGBoost control configuration:
    
    ```text
    device=cuda, tree_method=hist, max_depth=4, min_child_weight=50,
    eta=0.03, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8,
    lambda=10, alpha=0.1, max_bin=256, seed=20260809,
    max_rounds=3000, early_stopping=100
    ```
    
    Train corrected aggregate and causal-state direction, D/C mean, direct side quantile/probability, and adverse heads. If two pilot GPU runs do not produce identical canonical scores, switch all controls to CPU `hist`, `nthread=8`, and admit it only after byte identity.
    
    The primary model is pair-level and hard-capped at 1,000,000 parameters:
    
    - Six modality TCNs: six depthwise-separable causal blocks, width 32, kernel 5, dilations 1/2/4/8/16/32, SiLU, group norm, dropout 0.10, cropped to 240 seconds.
    - Slow two-layer GRU, width 128.
    - Two pre-normalized four-head attention layers, `d_model=128`, FFN width 256.
    - Shared state plus explicit LOW/HIGH query tokens; missing modalities are masked.
    - Slow state proposes direction; fast state supplies a bounded update:
    
    ```text
    s_D       = max(training MAD(D), 1 cent)
    D_hat     = s_D * (D_slow + 2*tanh(D_fast))
    C_hat     = median_T(C) + 2*MAD_T(C)*tanh(z_C)
    LOW_mean  = C_hat + D_hat
    HIGH_mean = C_hat - D_hat
    ```
    
    - Each side emits q50 plus softplus lower/upper gaps for noncrossing q10/q50/q90, a positive-net logit, and softplus adverse q90.
    - Run original and reflected inputs at inference, unreflect the second result, and average before calibration. LOW/HIGH reflection must swap side distributions exactly.
    
    Training uses deterministic PyTorch, AdamW `3e-4`, weight decay `1e-3`, cosine decay, at most 30 epochs, and early stopping after five. Sample sessions uniformly, then cutoffs. Use modality dropout and causal suffix masking.
    
    Loss weights:
    
    ```text
    paired direction BCE                 1.0
    direct side pinball                  1.0
    Smooth-L1 directional/common means  0.5
    side-positive BCE                    0.5
    payoff-weighted side ranking         0.5
    adverse q90 pinball                  0.5
    ```
    
    Clip ranking separation at the training-only p99; mask direction ties and censored targets. Do not use oracle teachers, LUPI, SSL, contrastive loss, or same-session future exemplars. Existing teacher experiments showed that unavailable future information did not transfer reliably. Same-information OOF distillation is allowed only after a champion already exists.
    
    ### Calibration and policy
    
    On each untouched calibration window:
    
    - Fit monotone beta calibration for each side’s `P(net>0)` with session-equal weights, deterministic L-BFGS, L2 regularization, and constrained positive slopes.
    - Add session-weighted nearest-rank residual corrections to q10/q50/q90 and adverse q90; apply deterministic monotone projection afterward.
    - A single-class, singular, nonconverged, or materially miscovered calibrator makes the scoring block abstain.
    - Report coverage and residual moments inside the eventual action region, not only over all dense rows.
    
    Policy:
    
    - Fixed until sufficient history: `P(net>0) ≥ 0.70`, `q10(net) > 0`, adverse q90 ≤ $200.
    - Also require `max(0, −realized_session_net) + adverse_q90 ≤ $750`.
    - From block start `c=272`, use the preceding 208–252 originally-causal OOF sessions. Search `P` in `{0.50,0.55,…,0.90}` and q10 percentile in `{50,60,70,80,90,95,97.5,99}`; the threshold is `max(0, nearest-rank percentile over valid prior side scores)`.
    - Replay every gate with exact chronology. Admissible gates require positive trailing mean and MDD ≤$750.
    - Maximize mean. Differences below $100/session are ties; then choose higher `P`, higher q10 percentile, fewer trades, and finally lower session variance.
    - If no gate qualifies, abstain for the block.
    - If both sides qualify, choose the larger quantized q10; exact ties abstain. Trade count remains emergent.
    
    ## 4. Fold-free proof, pivots, and escrow
    
    ### Prequential chronology
    
    Warmup blocks:
    
    | Score start | Fit | Calibration | Score |
    |---:|---|---|---|
    | 62, 83, 104 | `0..c−26`, fixed 10 epochs/rounds | `c−23..c−3` | next 21 |
    
    Two-session gaps separate fit/calibration and calibration/score.
    
    Official block `c`:
    
    ```text
    fit F:        0 .. c−49
    purge:        c−48, c−47
    early-stop E: c−46 .. c−26
    purge:        c−25, c−24
    calibrate C:  c−23 .. c−3
    purge:        c−2, c−1
    score S:      c .. min(c+20, 1002)
    ```
    
    There are 42 official starts `125..986`, scoring exactly sessions 125–1002: 878 sessions.
    
    Fit normalization on F only. Choose epoch/round count on F→E, restart from the same seed and refit exactly that count on `F ∪ E`, retain the F normalizer, calibrate on untouched C, and never refit after C.
    
    Fold roles:
    
    - F1–F5, sessions 125–750: all family, arm, policy, and pivot decisions.
    - F6, 751–876: one locked unattended sequential pass. Scheduled expanding refits may use earlier F6 outcomes causally, but no result or choice is disclosed until F6 closes.
    - F7, 877–1002: always contaminated-confirmatory and requires a committed `promotion: true` spec.
    - Block `c=734` crosses F5/F6. Development evaluates only through 750; freeze the champion, regenerate its boundary block, require byte identity through 750, and only then admit sealed 751–754 predictions to F6.
    - Block `c=860` crosses F6/F7. Keep 877–880 outcomes sealed until F7 authorization. Nonchampion boundary predictions are permanently `UNSCORED_FORBIDDEN`.
    
    ### Ablations and selection
    
    Run the cumulative XGBoost ladder through F1–F5:
    
    1. Corrected aggregate with explicit side.
    2. Slow state.
    3. Fast stock.
    4. Slow plus fast stock.
    5. Add IWM prints and surfaces.
    6. Add RUTW contextual state.
    7. Add OI/PIT rates/forward state.
    8. Add raw option quotes.
    
    Neural arms are limited to slow-only, fast-only, slow+stock, full-core, and full-quotes. Intermediate modality effects use deterministic masking diagnostics; retrain only material winners.
    
    For each family, compare against its parent using per-session Spearman rank correlation between predicted side margin and `directional_x2`, with payoff-weighted directional concordance and risk calibration as secondary metrics. Require:
    
    - One-sided paired circular-five-session bootstrap with Holm-adjusted `p < 0.05`.
    - Unadjusted 95% lower bound above zero.
    - Positive median fold effect and positive effect in at least four of F1–F5.
    - Runtime ≤20% of the recurring pipeline.
    - Final survival under leave-one-family-out.
    
    Dollar selection is permitted only over the pooled F1–F5 surface exceeding 200 sessions. Differences below $100/session cannot choose a champion; tie on simplicity, then lower variance.
    
    ### Promotion and assurance
    
    Promotion requires all:
    
    - Mean on 878 scored sessions ≥$2,000.
    - Zero-filled mean over all 1,003 sessions ≥$2,000; equivalently scored mean ≥$2,284.738041.
    - Cumulative zero-inclusive EOD MDD strictly below $1,000.
    - Positive total in every calendar year.
    - Contract leave-top-10 mean: remove ten highest daily nets and divide by 993; require ≥$2,000.
    - Report scored leave-top-10 divided by 868, trade distribution, median trades, top-day share, HHI, side mix, and all calibration coverage.
    - No cap, exact one-position chronology, and complete training/calibration provenance for every score row.
    
    Internal `HIGH_ASSURANCE` additionally requires a Rust year-stratified circular-five-session bootstrap, 10,000 replicates, warmup zeros fixed, seed `20260809`, and stateless SHA-256 counter sampling:
    
    - 5th percentile zero-filled mean ≥$2,000.
    - 95th percentile MDD <$1,000.
    - 5th percentile contract leave-top-10 ≥$2,000.
    - More than 90% of replicates jointly satisfy mean, MDD, leave-top-10, and every-year-positive gates.
    
    This is an internal robustness label, not a literal probability of future profit.
    
    ### Predeclared shortfall routing
    
    Use counterfactual replays at the model’s selected cutoffs:
    
    - Replace only the selected side with the true better side.
    - Replace only gate/timing with the true profitable timing.
    - Compare fixed 15-minute economics with the exact lawful path-exit oracle.
    
    Then route once:
    
    - Good same-time direction but weak replay: repair calibration, policy chronology, or risk.
    - Good direction/risk but poor fixed-15-minute economics: admit state-change exits only if the path-exit oracle at those same cutoffs has mean and leave-top-10 ≥$4,000 with every year positive.
    - Value between minute cutoffs: create a new causal transition action book only if its fresh executable oracle and leave-top-10 are both ≥$4,000.
    - Train-only signal: reduce capacity and strengthen session/reflection invariance.
    - Full core + both raw quote streams + one TCN + one rich analog + alignment controls all null: preregister exactly one committor/transition challenger. If null, stop internal feature churn and issue an external leading-data brief; do not use the old aggregate matrix to declare the raw corpus exhausted.
    
    Fixed 15-minute exits remain primary until a trigger fires.
    
    ### Forward escrow
    
    Planning incident disclosure: a wildcard OI layout inspection exposed 2026 schema and early-January timestamp metadata. No OI values, prices, outcomes, labels, or July-16+ score tranche were opened. The broader workspace cannot honestly claim zero 2026 contact; the July-16+ outcome exam remains unopened.
    
    Default SCORE cohort is the 17 expected exchange sessions from 2026-07-16 through 2026-08-07. The exact preceding 60 exchange sessions are `CONTEXT_ONLY`. Missing whole-session IWM authority remains a zero-trade denominator row and is never replaced. A later end date requires the user to commit that date and exact calendar list before any 2026 feature path opens.
    
    Before authorization:
    
    - Freeze and commit code, model, schema, normalizers, calibrator, gate, decision rules, metrics, path grammar, exact session roles, and expected outputs.
    
    After explicit authorization:
    
    1. Start a fresh process.
    2. Inventory only the frozen CONTEXT/SCORE day directories and hash allowed feature files.
    3. Audit every `openat/openat2` with `strace`; Rust rejects any path outside its typed role.
    4. CONTEXT files may seed OI/rate/seasonal state only. They cannot train, calibrate, select gates, or produce evaluated rows.
    5. Score sequentially and seal the score hash.
    6. Only after sealing, enable outcome-label paths for SCORE sessions and replay once.
    7. No retraining, threshold change, endpoint change, or retry.
    
    Escrow confirmation requires mean ≥$2,000/session and MDD <$1,000. Report uncertainty and sample size without changing the economic criteria.
    
    ## 5. Delivery workflow and minimum complete testing
    
    ### Bounded batches
    
    1. **Governance:** branch, reconcile `AGENTS.md` to the user’s Luna/Sol routing, commit the corrected plan/spec, repair the false evidence-ledger claim that raw quotes were already exhausted, add the legal research registry, arm registry, and isolated frozen Python lock.
    2. **Foundation:** source inventory, truth bridge, Rust evaluator, provenance, oracle/mutant/latency anchors.
    3. **Pilot compiler:** schema-era readers, clocks, 20-session core and quote publications, causal and performance gates.
    4. **Full substrate:** launch core and quote compilers through `lab/run.sh`; build model code against pilot outputs while compilation runs.
    5. **Controls:** fixed XGBoost ladder and F1–F5 family gates.
    6. **Primary proof:** fixed neural arms, LOFO, counterfactual localization, champion freeze, then locked F6 and authorized F7.
    7. **Escrow:** freeze, authorize, score, seal, and replay exactly once.
    
    Use the isolated Python 3.12.3 environment with only pinned direct requirements: NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.17.1, PyArrow 25, XGBoost 3.1.3, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128, safetensors 0.8, scikit-learn 1.7.2, and pytest 8.4.2. Do not use the conflicted omnibus environment or add `sktime`/TabPFN to the critical path.
    
    Representative neural block budget is ≤20 minutes; the projected 42-block champion run is ≤14 hours. Long jobs use PID/heartbeat/return-code receipts and exact-PID termination only.
    
    ### Minimal high-value test groups
    
    1. **Truth/evaluator:** explicit LOW→long/HIGH→short, parity mutation failure, exact joins/counts/formulas, censored/tie states, anchors, occupancy/side/cost mutants, zero-inclusive MDD, LTO.
    2. **Clock/causality:** post-cutoff perturbation leaves scores byte-identical; timezone/DST/double-shift mutants fail; strict-prior NBBO/spot; sweep totals unavailable early.
    3. **Ordering/schema:** shard and equal-time permutations are identical; source sequence is used only where authenticated; unit/schema/condition/venue/missing mutations affect only declared channels.
    4. **State/model:** reflection swaps distributions, masks are not zeros, parameter/storage caps, price-scale invariance, and two identical compiler/model runs produce identical canonical tensors and scores.
    5. **Scientific controls:** future-return leak succeeds strongly; shuffled labels, shifted streams, and session permutations collapse; aggregate and raw models share identical truth, calibration, policy, and evaluator.
    6. **Provenance/escrow:** dirty spec, existing destination, wrong input hash, missing fit receipt, forbidden path, preauthorization 2026 path, or outcome-before-score access all fail before publication.
    
    Every fixture must enter through production constructors. Each semantic detector must include a deliberately wrong mutant that is shown to fail. Run the grouped suite at milestone boundaries, not repetitive per-feature review loops. The clean baseline already passes all 148 existing `select_v2` targets.
    
    ### Anti-loop ownership
    
    - The root architect owns every scientific choice, task card, result interpretation, and final diff.
    - Use Luna/max only for exact mechanical batches. Use Sol/medium only for genuinely complex bounded implementation. Implementers receive files, interfaces, formulas, failure cases, commands, budgets, and expected outputs; they do not select architecture.

    - Concurrent worktrees are allowed only for disjoint, already-frozen interfaces.
    - No new abstraction ships unless used by at least two production call sites; maintain exactly one trainer, calibrator, evaluator, publication format, and model configuration.

    Yes. Their strongest value was in falsifying assumptions, not handing us a ready-made architecture.
    
    The useful overlap was:
    
    - Both independently confirmed that the current system never really tested the core hypothesis: side identity is missing from most emitted features, and the full raw options/stock state never reaches the learner.
    - Both identified the same causal reader failures: expiry shards are concatenated instead of time-merged, same-second stock state can be future relative to an option event, and vendor sweep totals can leak the completed sweep.
    - Opus made the clearest teacher/student point: an oracle teacher cannot transfer outcome information that is absent from the student’s causal inputs. That explains why privileged/oracle training looked sensible but collapsed out of sample.
    - Fable contributed a useful event-transition decomposition—location, effort without resolution, passive defense, control handoff—and argued for a small carrier tournament rather than committing immediately to one deep model.
    - Both forced the “correlation is not economics” correction: direction, payoff magnitude, adverse error placement, occupancy, and calibration must be evaluated separately. My own replay sensitivity confirmed that the same nominal accuracy can yield either strong profit or catastrophic drawdown depending on where errors occur.
    
    I am rejecting parts of both plans: their subjective success probabilities are not evidence, RTY payload violates the workspace law, passive-fill economics changes the contract, and neither supplied a sufficiently broad literature audit. I’m using their verified criticisms and testable mechanisms, not adopting either plan wholesale. I’m also reading the two `chat-plan` PDFs independently so those do not get conflated with the CLI plans.

    I’m adding a geographic and publisher-diversity lane:
    
    - Journal indexes/full text: PubMed/PMC, Europe PMC, DOAJ, OpenAIRE, Crossref, and publisher sites such as APS, IEEE, ACM, SIAM, PLOS, Nature, and Springer.
    - Legal manuscript recovery: Unpaywall links, author pages, university repositories, HAL, Zenodo, OSF, CORE/BASE, and national thesis repositories.
    - Non-US/UK sources: SciELO and Redalyc (Latin America), J-STAGE and CiNii (Japan), KCI/RISS (Korea), HAL/OpenAIRE (continental Europe), and legal Chinese institutional/journal portals where accessible.
    - Language handling: search in the source’s native terminology where practical, preserve the original title/abstract, and translate only for screening. Country and repository become audit columns so “international” is measured, not assumed.
    
    The current arXiv census remains one stratum, not the whole research sweep. After it finishes, I’ll run separate journal/repository strata and deduplicate by DOI/title.

    Agreed. “Broad” needs to be demonstrated, not asserted. I’m replacing the idea of a small fixed research matrix with an auditable saturation process.
    
    The finance lane will span equities/ETFs, single-name and index options, futures, rates, FX, commodities, volatility products, credit, electricity markets, crypto, auctions, and prediction markets. We are looking for transferable mechanisms—price discovery, inventory transfer, basis dislocations, liquidity recovery, informed flow, hedging feedback, and transition detection—not copying another asset’s strategy.

### 2026-08-09T14:49:09.601Z — ASSISTANT (ordinal 30394, id msg_0fbef113a6e13454016a78935524e08191aca2ee378845c796)

Provenance: line 30395, bytes [298718850,298721854), text SHA-256 `ba9bd0225e877a623aa2e3971750c1b24ded5765f33516963547d5d3bf918f4b`.

    I verified the old implementation. The teacher idea did not fail because teacher–student learning is inherently wrong; it failed because the old task violated the condition that makes distillation useful: the student must be able to infer the teacher’s decisions from its own inputs.
    
    What actually happened:
    
    - The LUPI teacher received `net_15m`, `mfe_15m`, and `mae_depth_15m`—future outcome variables. With those, the same network rose from causal rho `0.1473` to `0.2205`. That proves the network could express the ranking when handed future information.
    - The student received only the old 648-column aggregate matrix. Distillation cannot manufacture the teacher’s future variables; it can transfer only the part of the teacher logits predictable from those causal inputs. The best student scored `0.1380`, below the identical no-teacher model at `0.1473`.
    - The objective was also misaligned: it optimized within-session rank of a close-retention label, not paired `LOW_net` versus `HIGH_net`, calibrated side value, or the fixed-15-minute one-position replay.
    - The DP imitation arm learned on 146,710 oracle “flat” decisions but was scored on 482,456 action rows. The oracle’s value lived mostly in refusals: forcing a bad skipped action cost a median `$283`, while dropping a chosen action cost only `$24`. Many chosen bars were near-substitutes, so copying exact picks was unstable and the training/evaluation universes did not match.
    - The original LUPI shuffle guard was defective because it shuffled the label but left real teacher logits intact. The corrected guard passed, but the corrected student still underperformed the no-teacher control, so this bug does not rescue the result.
    - No economic replay was run for that lane; its reported dollar conversion was explicitly only a forecast.
    
    The human analogy is the key: a discretionary mentor does not merely say “this hindsight trade won.” They teach observable cues, context, uncertainty, counterfactuals, and why a setup should be refused. Our old teacher supplied answers without a causal explanation the student could see.
    
    I will retain teacher learning, but in a different role: after native raw experts establish learnable signal, the oracle supplies paired side advantage, common drag, adverse excursion, horizon value, and decision-regret targets; it also constructs time-matched hard positives/negatives. We will require each distilled target to improve held-out absolute side/value metrics over the same raw encoder without distillation. It will be an accelerator and regularizer—not a substitute for proving the causal information exists.

    Yes—the raw-data audit is the primary lane, not a side task. I have now inspected the clean readers and all six token-feed schemas across 2022–2025. Two important findings are already plan-changing:
    
    - The schema eras are not clean date eras. Stock-quote compact/wide profiles are interleaved through 2025; IWM option prints have two isolated wide-profile days; and some IWM option-quote session directories contain both compact and wide shards. So per-file schema/unit detection is mandatory.
    - The current clean readers discard much of what could make the state identifiable: stock `quote_timestamp`; option sequence/conditions/venues/ages; many higher Greeks; quote revisions; and causal sweep state. Existing negative models never saw that information correctly.
    
    I am not anchoring the plan on distillation. The decision order is:
    
    1. Verify truth, event generation, and evaluator.
    2. Compile the native causal state correctly.
    3. Measure where information exists—direction, timing/value, and risk separately—using matched nuisance/null controls.
    4. Choose the smallest surviving route: direct supervised experts, self-supervised event encoders, cross-modal alignment, event-conditioned candidates, horizon/exit modeling, or calibrated policy.
    5. Add oracle distillation only if it improves the same causal encoder over a matched non-distilled control.
    
    If distillation is null again, it is dropped. If direction remains weak but value/risk/timing are strong, we route toward selective abstention, event timing, longer occupancy, or state-change exits instead of forcing a side classifier. The final plan will follow what the raw tests support, not a favorite modeling idea.

### 2026-08-09T14:58:58.038Z — ASSISTANT (ordinal 30597, id msg_0fbef113a6e13454016a7895a3d45481919d72bdc104e0e6de)

Provenance: line 30598, bytes [299732649,299734966), text SHA-256 `d48df2a6d90460f91c32a0ffbfbd18c876aba47aa6c3afb20813e9ceeb60d47d`.

    Yes—this is one of the strongest remaining hypotheses.
    
    A snapshot can tell us “price is at an extreme.” It cannot tell us whether that extreme was formed by:
    
    - orderly initiative flow,
    - an exhausted sweep followed by absorption/refill,
    - a liquidity vacuum,
    - repeated failed pushes,
    - accelerating cross-stream confirmation,
    - or a noisy spike that immediately continues.
    
    Those states can have nearly identical current price, IV, flow totals, and OI geometry while implying different futures. The order, response delay, persistence, and recovery path are the information. Our cached minute-summary tests largely erased exactly that.
    
    The native model should therefore predict more than “LOW or HIGH wins.” At each causal cutoff it should estimate:
    
    - reversal versus continuation,
    - hazard/time until the current extreme is displaced,
    - side value at several horizons,
    - common drag,
    - adverse excursion,
    - and whether the setup is mature enough to act or should remain an abstention.
    
    The fair test is not “neural sequence model versus XGBoost.” It is:
    
    - same channels, same folds, same labels, same capacity budget;
    - current-state-only encoder versus history encoder;
    - then time-order destruction, within-stream reversal, and cross-stream lag perturbations.
    
    A path effect survives only if the history model beats the snapshot control and its gain disappears when the meaningful event order is destroyed while marginals remain intact.
    
    My current architectural lean is a two-speed causal model: a compact event-time/one-second encoder over the last few minutes plus a slow session-to-date state. I’m not yet locking GRU versus TCN/state-space; the peer audit and recent irregular-sequence research are being used to choose one frozen probe. But yes: if the question is how the extreme developed and whether it is finishing, a causal sequence representation is much more faithful than another aggregate matrix.

    Exactly. The useful unit is likely not “the last 240 seconds” as one undifferentiated block, but an event-centered formation episode:
    
    - approach: how price and flow reached the candidate extreme;
    - contact: what happened at/near it—aggression, absorption, quote withdrawal/refill, options/stock agreement;
    - response: whether continuation attempts failed and displacement began.
    
    That suggests a causal sequence encoder with explicit phase/time-to-touch information and separate reversal, continuation, and “not yet confirmed” hazards. One hard rule: confirmation evidence must occur before the executable cutoff. If confirmation needs events after the current cutoff, we must create a later action with a fresh executable label; we cannot quietly feed that response into the earlier action. I’m adding a direct event-centered sequence-versus-snapshot test to the research gate.

    Yes—and that reframes the learning problem more cleanly. Direction is not an arbitrary class to discover:
    
    - candidate LOW → proposed long;
    - candidate HIGH → proposed short;
    - the model’s job is to decide whether that proposed extreme is actually becoming a reversal, is still unresolved, or is failing into continuation.
    
    So the primary sequence target should be a competing-state/hazard target such as `confirmed reversal`, `invalidated/continuation`, or `unresolved`, plus expected net and adverse excursion. That is closer to how a discretionary tape reader operates than asking a model to predict a generic return sign. I’m checking the production event constructor now to pin exactly when the candidate extreme exists and which pre/post-touch observations are legally available.

    The ~$4,179 and ~$5,735 figures are valid outcome oracles, but they are not evidence that a causal model can earn those amounts.
    
    The key distinction is:
    
    - ~$5,735/session: with hindsight, choose the best realized action from a dense grid of roughly 771 candidates per session while respecting one-position chronology.
    - ~$4,179/session: another hindsight policy over those realized outcomes.
    - Unknown causal ceiling: what can be selected using only information genuinely available at each cutoff.
    
    Because the action grid offers long and short opportunities almost every minute, hindsight can capture favorable randomness that no model could predict. The oracle proves there is enough economic opportunity and that the evaluator can express large profits. It does not prove what fraction is identifiable from the raw state.
    
    That does not rule out either target:
    
    - $2,000 is about 35% of the $5,735 oracle.
    - $3,000 is about 52%.
    - Under the zero-filled 1,003-session contract, $2,000 requires about $2,285 over the 878 scored sessions; $3,000 requires about $3,427 over them.
    
    My honest current assessment is:
    
    - $3,000 remains possible.
    - $2,000 remains possible.
    - Neither is yet demonstrated probable.
    - The old aggregate, OI, and oracle-distillation results cannot answer this because they either discarded the raw causal state or measured misleading within-session ranking.
    - The raw sequence/path representation has not yet received the decisive side-aware, causal, equal-population test needed to estimate the achievable ceiling.
    
    The revised plan will therefore treat $2,000 as the mandatory promotion floor and $3,000 as the frozen champion’s next target. Before committing to a large model build, it will estimate the causal ceiling using out-of-session predictions from the actual stock and options streams, explicit LOW/HIGH direction, identical snapshot/sequence controls, matched nulls, and exact economic replay. That test—not the hindsight oracle—will tell us whether the bottleneck is representation, candidate timing, exits, or genuinely unavailable information.

    The teacher/oracle question now has a precise answer. The prior teacher was strong only because it saw the future outcome itself; the student saw 648 old aggregate columns that did not contain enough repeatable side information. Distillation therefore asked the student to reproduce variation that was not observable from its inputs, and it underperformed the same model trained directly on labels. The oracle-policy imitation was even less aligned: most oracle value came from refusing trades and choosing among near-substitute future-dependent schedules, while its training and scoring universes did not match.
    
    That does not kill privileged learning. It changes its role: first demonstrate that a causal raw encoder recovers side/timing information; then test distillation against an identical label-only student. If teacher logits add no held-out paired-direction and replay value, the teacher lane is killed immediately. Outcome labels remain useful as value, adverse-excursion, and regret supervision—not as proof that the answer was visible at decision time.

    That is exactly the right correction. IV should not enter as a generic “surface feature” and then be left for a tree to discover its use. Its strongest role may be to change what the tape means.
    
    The trader-mechanistic version I’m adding is a small, preregistered volatility-conditioned response block:
    
    - Convert price distance, progress, reversal, and time into forecast-variance units: “how much of the expected move has been consumed?” and “was this response unusually weak or strong for today’s volatility?”
    - Measure stock impact surprise: realized price response to aggressive flow minus the response expected from current volatility, spread, and depth. Heavy buying with abnormally weak progress is an absorption/exhaustion signal; the mirrored case applies at highs.
    - Re-express option activity in delta/vega/gamma-equivalent risk, divided by contemporaneous option depth and the forward-volatility budget.
    - Separate mechanical option-price movement from repricing: subtract the causal Greek-predicted change from observed bid/ask change. The residual tells us whether implied volatility itself is lifting, fading, or refusing to confirm the tape.
    - Use independently inverted bid-IV and ask-IV, not only midpoint IV. Widening or asymmetric IV on the aggressive side can distinguish genuine urgency from price changes caused merely by spot delta.
    - Test cross-stream confirmation explicitly: stock reversal plus IV/quote response must beat the same streams time-shifted or order-permuted. If it survives, it becomes the fusion layer; if it does not, we kill the interaction rather than add dozens of academic indicators.
    
    This is one coherent mechanism family, not another feature soup. It directly represents the discretionary sequence—approach, contact, defense, depletion, handoff—but measures whether each response is exceptional relative to the market’s current implied and forecast volatility.

    You’re right—I treated your example too literally. IV-conditioned tape is one interaction, not the framework.
    
    The correct unit is a market-state mechanism, built from all streams together:
    
    - Location and path: where price is in the session, how it approached the candidate area, speed/curvature, failed progress, retests, and the sequence of local highs/lows.
    - Stock response: quotes, displayed liquidity changes, trades, venue/condition, aggressive flow, impact, replenishment, and whether price responds as expected.
    - IWM option response: prints, quote revisions, call/put and strike migration, DTE, sweep completion, bid/ask pressure, Greek-equivalent risk, IV repricing, and whether options confirm or reject the stock move.
    - RUTW context: the same response logic on the index-weekly stream, used as context—not execution—and tested for genuine lead/confirmation rather than correlation.
    - Slow state: full IV surface and higher-Greek topology, forward-volatility distribution, realized-versus-implied budget, session regime, prior-known OI scenarios, and lawful rates.
    - Transition state: not “is there absorption?” but “did approach → contact → defense → attacker depletion → handoff actually progress?” A transition/committor head estimates whether the state is moving toward a completed low, completed high, continuation, or no-trade state.
    - Cross-stream innovations: model the expected response of each stream from the others, then use the residual. Unexpected non-response, delayed response, divergence, or synchronized handoff is often more informative than any raw level.
    - Confidence and contradiction: experts may abstain; the fusion layer must know when stock, options, surface, and index context disagree rather than averaging them into noise.
    
    That also exposes a defect in the current path probe: it contains microstructure responses but omits an explicit one-second stock-price return/path channel and session-location context. A tape model without the approach path cannot represent the discretionary decision you described. I’m stopping that design before the full run and replacing it with a shared causal price/location/clock backbone that every modality expert conditions on. The experiment will ask what each raw stream adds over the same path context, then whether synchronized cross-stream interactions add more.

    You’re right. I failed that instruction in the same way you warned me about: I anchored on the inherited TCN plan, then overreacted to your IV example instead of independently re-deriving where information could exist. That is not the level of thinking you asked for.
    
    I’m correcting the planning frame now. The research object is not a list of features or even a list of feeds. It is the latent decision state a trader needs:
    
    - Where is the market in its path?
    - Which side is supplying or demanding liquidity?
    - How elastic is price to that pressure?
    - Is pressure being absorbed, exhausted, or handed off?
    - Is a reversal/continuation transition becoming more likely?
    - How much volatility/range budget remains?
    - Which observations contradict the proposed trade?
    - How uncertain is the state estimate?
    
    From that, I independently see several representation routes that the inherited plan did not adequately test:
    
    - Event/variance time: represent the approach and response by information arrivals or accumulated forecast variance, not only fixed seconds. The same economic phase can last 3 seconds on one day and 90 seconds on another.
    - Cross-stream predictive innovations: train each stream to predict the next lawful state of the others, then trade on unexpected response/non-response. This can expose hidden pressure that raw concatenation misses.
    - Competing-risk committors: directly estimate the causal probability of reaching an up transition, down transition, or no-trade state before the other—not merely regress a 15-minute return.
    - Multiscale path geometry: use causal path signatures/change-point likelihoods to represent ordering across several scales without hand-enumerating windows.
    - Latent-state filtering: update a small state-space belief over approach, defense, depletion, handoff, continuation, and ambiguity as events arrive; the model may abstain when evidence conflicts.
    - Causal day/phase alignment: align session prefixes by their observed development rather than clock time, attacking the repeatedly observed failure where within-day ranks do not transfer to absolute cross-day values.
    - Decision-focused occupancy learning: after recoverability is established, train selection against the one-position opportunity cost rather than treating every minute as an independent classification row.
    
    IV, quotes, tape, Greeks, OI, RUTW, and price path are sensors inside those hypotheses—not the hypotheses themselves. I am expanding the final proof into a small representation tournament over these distinct ideas, each with a matching destruction test, rather than assuming the TCN wins in advance.
    
    One useful independent result has already landed: the existing forward-volatility model has real folds-4/5 variance skill, but it is far narrower than we thought—it uses one non-0DTE IWM ATM IV row, no RUTW, no third-order Greeks, and no rich surface. Its publication also has thousands of duplicate `(day, horizon)` rows and silently picks stale folds. So the right conclusion is neither “ignore it” nor “reuse it”: repair its OOF publication, then use it as a volatility/phase clock and risk sensor while testing richer distributional heads.

### 2026-08-09T16:54:36.954Z — ASSISTANT (ordinal 33283, id msg_0fbef113a6e13454016a78b0ba854081918a4d4aa69e11880d)

Provenance: line 33285, bytes [348374009,348378412), text SHA-256 `be8c6b1c8c3bc23d2de8a371d8bfb236d2ddb5a40a4c92bb6337ef74cd88009b`.

    Agreed. The mistake would be to keep asking, “What interactions can I manufacture from these columns?” A trader thinks across the entire decision, and the raw data can improve every part of it—not only the predictor.
    
    Here is the broader first-principles map I’m using now:
    
    - Where to pay attention: build a causal liquidity landscape from session path, prior highs/lows, VWAP, opening range, option strike concentration, quote-depth discontinuities, and volatility-scaled distance. This defines watch zones before a trade exists.
    - How price arrives: distinguish impulse, orderly auction, grind, stop-run, and repeated failed probes using event/variance time, impact per unit flow, spread/depth evolution, venue/size persistence, and path curvature.
    - What happens at contact: infer defense, withdrawal, replenishment, exhaustion, or acceptance from the joint sequence of price progress, quote removals/additions, aggressive prints, option-book response, and cross-root confirmation.
    - Who appears to be persistent: infer latent metaorders or inventory urgency from condition, venue, size, fragmentation, recurrence, and response—not by assuming “large print = informed.”
    - Whether the market is repricing direction or only volatility: decompose option moves into mechanical delta/gamma effects versus genuine IV/skew/term repricing, and compare call/put and IWM/RUTW behavior.
    - Where the market has room to travel: use the dynamic liquidity/strike landscape, forecast distribution, and nearby opposing pressure to estimate open space and choose 15/30/60/120-minute value rather than forcing every setup into 15 minutes.
    - When the thesis has completed or failed: exit on a state transition—loss of defense, renewed acceptance, opposing handoff, consumed volatility budget, or arrival at the next liquidity cluster—not merely a fixed clock once entry skill exists.
    - When not to trade: use contradiction among experts, poor data quality, excessive adverse-excursion quantiles, high cost/expected-move ratio, or ambiguous transition state as explicit abstention evidence.
    - How to learn across days: align similar causal prefixes by auction phase and variance consumed, rather than assuming 10:07 on two days is the same state.
    - How to generate better candidates: if the dense minute grid proves unnecessarily hard, create entries only when a causal transition detector moves from WATCH to CONFIRMED, then build fresh executable labels and first prove that candidate set’s oracle ceiling exceeds the floor.
    
    Several novel raw-data constructions follow from that map independently of your IV example:
    
    - A liquidity-elasticity field: expected price movement per unit aggressive stock/options pressure at each state; abnormal non-response is the signal.
    - A two-scenario hedging-pressure band: update unsigned OI plus signed customer flow under both dealer-sign assumptions, then keep only conclusions robust to both.
    - Cross-stream predictive residuals: what IWM stock, IWM options, and RUTW should have done given the other streams versus what they actually did.
    - A causal “auction committor”: probability that the developing state completes a low, completes a high, continues through, or remains ambiguous.
    - Metaorder persistence and decay: whether venue/size/condition clusters continue exerting pressure or have exhausted.
    - Dynamic barrier/accelerant topology: whether nearby strikes and liquidity pools are absorbing movement or, once crossed, creating open space.
    - Phase-aligned analogs: retrieve prior session prefixes with the same causal development and measure their subsequent outcome distribution without using the current future.
    - Multi-horizon value as a competing decision: side, entry, horizon, and abstention are learned jointly under occupancy, not as separate afterthoughts.
    
    This is now the architecture-selection basis. The current raw proofs become sensors and controls inside it; they no longer predetermine that a fixed-second TCN or fixed-15-minute trade is the answer.

    The negatives are telling us something specific: we have mostly been asking the wrong prediction question.
    
    The current action book asks, at almost every minute, “which side will have the better fixed-horizon return?” That is essentially dense short-horizon market direction. Most minutes are not genuine discretionary entry states, so rare approach→contact→response transitions are diluted by hundreds of inert/noisy rows per day. A hindsight oracle can still pick the winners, which makes its ceiling look enormous, but that does not make the dense minute label identifiable.
    
    The main mistakes have been:
    
    - Target mismatch: fixed 15-minute return and fixed take-profit instead of “has a reversal/continuation transition occurred, and is it still continuing?”
    - Candidate mismatch: scoring every minute and both sides instead of scoring causally detected transition states.
    - Representation loss: earlier matrices erased side, event order, response/non-response, and cross-stream timing.
    - Modality misuse: IV, OI, Greeks, and option quotes mostly describe volatility, positioning, liquidity, and risk; asking them to vote direction additively is weak. Their value is conditional interaction with stock/tape response.
    - Signal dilution: training loss is dominated by ordinary minutes rather than clean low-MAE entry states.
    - Optimization uncertainty: the quote TCN is deliberately tiny/one epoch; its same-architecture leak control is still running so we do not confuse undertraining with absence of signal.
    
    The valid future-leak controls already prove the truth join and replay can express profitable behavior. What remains is to ask the causal data the trader-shaped question: at a detected extreme, did aggressive pressure fail, did defense/refill hold, did the opposite side take control, and what is the competing hazard now? The joint stock/options path test is being revised around exactly that target, plus 30/60-minute heads so a noisy 15-minute label cannot falsely kill the data. If that still fails, the dense candidate clock—not another feature family—is what we replace.

### 2026-08-09T19:34:56.712Z — ASSISTANT (ordinal 37850, id msg_0fbef113a6e13454016a78d658d2788191921d41b02b71b54e)

    The broad bottleneck is now clearer: we have mostly modeled “what the market state is.” A discretionary entry is based on a counterfactual: given the aggression and available liquidity, did price respond as it normally should?
    
    That means the decisive variables are not raw flow, refill, IV, or quote size. They are:
    
    - effort versus result: adverse aggression minus the price impact it should normally produce;
    - defense persistence: whether displayed liquidity recovers after being hit, conditional on pressure;
    - depletion: whether repeated aggression produces progressively less movement;
    - transfer-of-control: whether desired-side aggression suddenly produces more movement;
    - cross-stream confirmation/refusal: whether options, IV, and RUTW react as expected when IWM changes state;
    - the change in those relationships from approach → contact → confirmation.
    
    This is a system-identification problem, not a feature-laundry-list problem. The model should first learn each stream’s expected causal response from prior sessions, then trade the residual innovations and changing response elasticities. That also attacks the cross-session generalization failure because it removes raw level/regime scale.
    
    If that exact event-level representation is still null, the next conclusion is not “try more features.” It means dc010 is the wrong decision event. Then we replace the price-threshold candidate with a causal state-transition clock that fires when defense → depletion → transfer-of-control is actually observed. That is the only candidate redesign I will permit before closing the on-disk entry case.

    <proposed_plan>
    # Native Evidence Entry Program to the $1,600 Floor
    
    ## 1. Contract and scientific position
    
    - Build from clean `select-v2@ab3940bc`. This program covers entries only; causal exits remain a later project.
    - Primary entry certificate: uncapped hindsight `clean_pre_refail_MFE` value, its timestamp, and marked-net MAE. This is chosen now from the user’s “perfect entries first” intent—not after seeing results.
    - Barrier outcomes at 5/10/15/20 bps and fixed terms at 1/2/5/10/15/30/60/120 minutes and close are auxiliary labels and robustness panels. None may replace the primary certificate or become a selected take-profit.
    - Binding entry bar, in both development blocks:
      - one-sided 95% session-bootstrap lower bound ≥ $1,600/session;
      - zero-inclusive EOD MDD < $1,000;
      - zero selected trades with marked-net MAE > $300;
      - uncapped one-position chronology, all zero-trade days included, costs embedded once;
      - leave-top-10-out, min-year, and min-half-year concentration gates also pass.
    - Correct the language: executable availability has been measured; causal predictability from the exact lossless prefix has not. Opportunity does not prove learnability.
    - This build reads sessions 125–749 only. Session 750 is explicitly unavailable because its physical row group includes prohibited later sessions. Report dev-B as 625–749, never as the complete registered fold 5. Fold 6, fold 7, 2026, RTY, and escrow remain untouched.
    
    ## 2. Build the exact shared authority
    
    - Add a lossless production quote API alongside the unchanged legacy API:
      - price: `MISSING | NONPOSITIVE | POSITIVE_U6`;
      - size: `MISSING | NEGATIVE_OR_BAD | ZERO | POSITIVE_SHARES`;
      - optional condition code, raw Frame-B time, converted Frame-A time, physical profile, and row ordinal;
      - eligible iff both conditions are `Some(0)`, both prices are positive, and ask ≥ bid; size never gates;
      - malformed schema, nonfinite values, overflow, or ambiguous units fail closed.
    - Prove legacy/new bridging on the probe: changed members, best-quote timestamps, envelope differences, and legacy byte identity. The legacy even-sum midpoint filter must never enter the new execution authority.
    - Seal `EVENT_PIVOT_SOURCE` for sessions 125–749 using per-session counts and sequence roots. Never hash or decode across the mixed session-750 source boundary.
    - Keep labels quote-only. Build feature spines for trades, option prints, Greeks, OI, and rates separately; prove those streams are unreachable from the label constructor.
    - Publish factorized natural-key authorities, based on the verified safe census:
      - `DECISION_MAP`: 13,942,529 all-policy D1/D2 decisions;
      - `ENTRY_PATH`: 481,678 unique `(session, cutoff, side)` entry paths;
      - `PIVOT_LABEL`: 13,942,529 `(entry key, governing signal)` pivot labels;
      - missing or duplicate joins abort; the manifest shows the exact 43.9372% cell-reduction arithmetic.
    - B-grid and C/D clocks receive separate entry-path leaves because their instants are outside the measured A-clock key domain.
    - Decode each session once, materialize eligible quote-envelope arrays, and use range-query/segment-tree labeling rather than rescanning future paths per decision.
    - Exact label law:
      - fresh entry is the first eligible group strictly after cutoff;
      - LOW enters at `ask_max`; HIGH at `bid_min`;
      - favorable/adverse envelopes remain side-specific;
      - pivot refail includes the entry group; favorable search starts afterward;
      - same-group favorable/refail ties are adverse;
      - cost is applied once.
    - Separate deterministic scientific files from runtime/PID/RSS receipts; stage and publish atomically with no replacement and two-run byte identity.
    
    ## 3. Candidate clocks and seven-cell staircase
    
    Candidate clocks:
    
    - A: all 12 TOL2 D1/D2 policy strata; no outcome-crowned policy.
    - B: shared evidence-WAIT grid at 0/30/60/120 seconds from exact visibility. ENTER uses a newly priced current entry; otherwise WAIT and rescore; PASS occurs at invalidation or after 120 seconds. No hindsight-optimal wait target.
    - C: displayed top-of-book control transfer—pressure, depletion, same-price refill before concession, desired aggressor, and first stock response. Never claim queue or participant identity.
    - D: best-quote withdrawal—emit an unsigned withdrawal event plus withdrawn-side covariate. The conventional ask→LONG/bid→SHORT mapping is diagnostic, not hard-coded truth.
    - E: option-led clock remains `BLOCKED` until exact contract, direction, deliverable/multiplier, underlier, and timestamp authority exists. No surrogate clock.
    
    Before fitting, every clock receives its own density, latency, take-all, perfect chronological/WIS opportunity, MAE, concentration, and required-discrimination/coverage curve under the primary clean-MFE certificate. A clock whose perfect lower-bound opportunity cannot fund $1,600 cannot stand alone, but C/D may remain evidence features in A/B.
    
    Run at most seven preregistered cells:
    
    1. `R_A`: side-aware role/statistical ruler on A, including the same-row aggregate twin.
    2. `R_B`: the same ruler shared across the four WAIT instants.
    3. `R_C`: cheap standalone ruler only if C’s opportunity and effective sample size can fund a powered test.
    4. `R_D`: same rule for D.

    OI and rates remain slow known-at context and do not receive a dedicated first-wave cell. Analog retrieval is removed from the critical path.
    
    ## 4. Controls, evaluation, and stop rules
    
    - Enforce a side-representation registry: each field is market-frame, candidate-oriented, unsigned, or ambiguous. Emit explicit side identity and candidate-oriented transforms; ambiguous fields cannot support a directional claim.
    - Required model controls:

Publish the measured gap and move the next decision to genuinely new unexecuted-demand data—not another renamed feature pass.

    <proposed_plan>
    # Fresh-Entry Evidence-Window Rebuild
    
    ## Summary
    
    Rebuild from clean `select-v2@ab3940bc`. Historical event models, candidate-row tests, pre-cutoff entries, and fixed-horizon matrices are evidence only; they cannot validate this design.
    
    The scientific object is one causal session-time decision with `LOW`, `HIGH`, or `PASS`. Candidate IDs are evidence tokens—not samples or trades. The entry certificate deliberately uses hindsight MFE exits because entry selection is the current objective; it is explicitly nondeployable until exits are designed later.
    
    Binding goals:
    
    - Primary floor: at least $1,600 mean net/session.
    - Next rung: $2,000; aspiration: $3,000.
    - Uncapped, chronological, one-position replay.
    - Cumulative zero-inclusive EOD MDD below $1,000.
    - Zero selected trades with marked-net MAE above $300.
    - Primary final denominator remains zero-filled all 1,003 registered sessions; scored-session results are secondary.
    - No claim of greater-than-90% success confidence until the new oracle and observability gates actually pass.
    
    All implementation and scientific runs begin in a fresh clean lane because the current planning lane is contaminated by a prohibited 2026 Parquet-footer inspection.
    
    ## 1. Build the exact decision and label authority first
    
    Add immutable Rust publications and these explicit interfaces:
    
    - `EvidenceToken`: authenticated side, visibility time, policy/scale, age, location/evidence quality and typed source state.
    - `DecisionKey`: session plus exact decision timestamp.
    - `FreshEntryLabel`: side, strict-after entry, hindsight-MFE exit, net, time-to-MFE, MAE-through-MFE and typed availability state.
    - `ModelScores`: value, risk, timing and scheduling-advantage distributions for both sides.
    - `ReplayTrade`: decision, entry, exit, realized net, MAE and equity effects.
    
    Decision construction:
    
    - A side becomes eligible when authenticated same-side evidence becomes visible. Each token remains active for 120 seconds, implementing the allowed one-to-two-bar confirmation period.
    - Consecutive D1/D2 rows carrying the same evidence update one ragged evidence set; they never become duplicate trades.
    - Score once at every whole-second boundary inside the union of active windows and at every intrasecond evidence-set change.
    - `LOW` authorizes long and `HIGH` authorizes short. Opposite-side evidence remains contextual. If neither side is active, the primary policy cannot enter.
    - At intrasecond decisions, snapshot partial-second state exactly at the decision timestamp. A completed-second row may never substitute for it.
    
    Fresh labels:
    
    - Entry is the first eligible IWM quote group strictly after the decision.
    - Eligibility requires bid/ask conditions both equal zero, positive two-sided prices and `ask >= bid`; displayed size never gates execution.
    - Equal-millisecond rows are unordered envelopes:
      - long entry `ask_max`, favorable mark `bid_max`, adverse mark `bid_min`;
      - short entry `bid_min`, favorable mark `ask_min`, adverse mark `ask_max`.
    - Exit is the earliest full-RTH executable MFE. MAE is the worst marked-net loss from entry through that exit.
    - Use integer arithmetic only:
    
      `frac_u6 = trunc_toward_zero(move_u6 × 1,000,000 / entry_u6)`
    
      `net_cent = frac_u6 × 10 − 576`
    
      Cost is deducted exactly once; spread is already embedded in executable fills.
    - Publish fixed horizons and barriers only as diagnostics. Candidate-specific pivot/refail exits and realized-MAE eligibility filters are forbidden in the primary certificate.
    
    Before feature work, compute exact risk-qualified weighted-interval oracles for:
    
    - active evidence windows;
    - all RTH seconds as the unrestricted candidate-coverage comparator;
    - standalone entries delayed by 60 and 120 seconds;
    - a joint value/risk corruption curve showing the discrimination needed to meet the contract.
    
    The feature build is GREEN only when the active-window oracle’s one-sided 95% session-bootstrap lower bound is at least $3,200/session in both F4 and truncated F5. This is twice the floor, requiring no more than 50% oracle-value capture.
    
    - If active windows fail but all-RTH clears $3,200, broaden the causal decision mask before modeling.
    - If even all-RTH is below $1,600, this entry certificate cannot meet the floor.
    - Results between $1,600 and $3,200 establish physical possibility but cannot support the requested high-confidence claim.
    
    ## 2. Compile one causal multistream substrate
    
    Extend the existing readers additively; legacy APIs remain byte-identical.
    
    - Stock quotes retain conditions, exchanges, deltas, row order and separate typed price/size states. Missing, nonpositive, zero and valid values never collapse.
    - Stock prints retain trade and quote timestamps, sequence, conditions, attached NBBO and quality. `price_lead_1` remains structurally banned.
    - Option prints retain exact contract identity, all timestamps, conditions, quote state, sweeps, vendor IV, every Greek through third order and all available flow fields. Attached-quote signing is primary; vendor side and alternative signers are disagreement channels.
    - Option quotes retain all conditions, sizes, deltas and exchanges, and perform a timestamp k-way merge across expiry shards.
    - Calendar admission and session range are resolved before any path is formed. Every timestamp crosses the existing `SessionClock` boundary exactly once.
    
    One streaming pass reads every admitted token and emits nonduplicated session stores, each capped at 64 channels:
    
    - Candidate evidence: ragged DeepSets tokens representing location, evidence age, scale, ancestry and quality.
    - Stock tape: aggression, quote additions/removals/refill, depth/spread, arrival structure, effort-versus-response elasticity, exhaustion and control handoff.
    - Option prints: signed pressure, maturity/moneyness partitions, sweeps, Greek-weighted flow, IV innovation, unresolved-flow aging and mechanical Taylor-price residuals.
    - Option quotes: refill/fade, contract response, width and print-to-quote confirmation/refusal.
    - Slow context: repaired forward-vol expected-move clock, vendor IV surface/skew/term state, higher Greeks, prior-known OI, RUTW disagreement and typed availability.
    
    The discretionary framework is an explicit continuous baseline:
    
    `LOCATION → APPROACH/CONTACT → DEFENSE → AGGRESSOR DEPLETION → CONTROL HANDOFF`
    
    Absorption alone is not an entry. The learned model may combine simultaneous evidence across streams beyond what a human can monitor.
    
    Local FRED files are current-vintage context only. They cannot authorize exact historical American bid/ask-IV inversion. Initial mechanics use observed vendor IV/Greeks, raw option prices, vega-normalized widths and Taylor price residuals. Exact own-IV remains typed `BLOCKED` until point-in-time rate, distribution, borrow and series-term inputs exist.
    
    Worst-case storage is approximately 14 GiB for four dense 64-channel stores plus roughly 1.5 GiB for ragged evidence—under `/workspace`, never `/tmp`.
    
    ## 3. Run one bounded model tournament
    
    Use identical rows, folds, normalizers, prediction heads and replay for every arm:
    
    1. Continuous discretionary XGBoost baseline.
    2. Direct causal sequence model.
    3. The same sequence model with fold-local predictive-innovation pretraining.
    4. Fixed prior-session analog retrieval on the learned causal embedding.
    5. Cross-fitted full-episode privileged teacher distillation, run last.
    
    The causal model is fixed at approximately 100,600 parameters, hard-capped at 150,000:
    
    - side-equivariant DeepSets-64 evidence encoder;
    - separate time-aware GRU-64 experts for stock, option prints and option quotes;
    - context MLP-64;
    - additive heads first;
    - six fixed rank-8 interactions:
      - evidence × stock;
      - evidence × option prints;
      - stock × option prints;
      - context × stock;
      - context × option prints;
      - option quotes × option prints.
    
    A weak marginal result cannot kill one of these declared interactions. Each interaction must beat its additive comparator and collapse under a marginal-preserving alignment destruction.
    
    Direct, equally normalized objectives are:
    
    - net-to-hindsight-MFE quantiles;
    - MAE-through-MFE quantiles and `P(MAE > $300)`;
    - time-to-MFE;
    - oracle scheduling advantage;
    - paired LOW-versus-HIGH ranking.
    
    The teacher sees resolved full episodes only while generating cross-fitted training targets. At inference the student receives causal prefixes only. It survives only if it beats the identical direct student by more than $100/session in both outer blocks and a shifted-teacher target does not reproduce the gain.
    
    Train three fixed seeds per arm, four GPU fits concurrently, in two waves. Ten epochs cover 146.25 million session-second tokens per fit.
    
    ## 4. Calibrate and evaluate the actual entry policy
    
    Use two-session embargoes:
    
    - F4: train 125–497, embargo 498–499, test 500–624.
    - Truncated F5: train 125–622, embargo 623–624, test 625–749.
    
    Generate prequential calibration predictions from sessions 250–497 and 250–622 respectively, providing more than 200 prior sessions without using outer outcomes.
    
    At each flat decision:
    
    - form a one-sided 90% lower bound on scheduling advantage;
    - form a session-simultaneous upper band for MAE;
    - enter only if advantage lower bound is positive, MAE upper band is at most $300, and current drawdown plus predicted risk remains below $1,000;
    - choose the unique better qualifying side; exact ties or nonfinite values mean `PASS`;
    - impose no trade-count cap;
    - remain occupied until the certificate’s true MFE exit.
    
    Required controls:
    
    - within-session label shuffle;
    - true side reflection and per-side metrics;
    - equal-information unordered bag and within-time permutation;
    - between-time order destruction;
    - nonwrapping stream shift;
    - option-contract mismatch;
    - future-leak and synthetic-XOR positive controls;
    - post-decision payload mutation;
    - two-run byte identity.
    
    Family promotion requires Holm-corrected rank improvement, consistent sign across folds, and at least $100/session economic improvement. Final keeps require leave-one-family-out confirmation.
    
    Champion acceptance requires, independently in F4 and truncated F5:
    
    - one-sided 95% session-bootstrap lower bound at least $1,600/session;
    - zero actual selected-trade MAE breaches above $300;
    - cumulative zero-inclusive EOD MDD below $1,000;
    - every test day included, including zero-trade days;
    - leave-top-10-out and minimum half-block concentration reported;
    - distances to $2,000 and $3,000 reported.
    
    After the specification and model are frozen, run one unchanged fold-6 confirmation. Fold 7 remains contaminated-confirmatory. No 2026 payload opens without the separate escrow authorization.
    
    ## 5. Delivery discipline and tests
    
    Implementation order:
    
    1. Lossless readers, safe event prefix and immutable authority.
    2. Strict-after labels, independent oracle/replay implementations and the $3,200 gate.
    3. Streaming feature stores and model harness in parallel once the gate is green.
    4. Five-arm tournament, calibration and exact replay.
    5. One adversarial review, one consolidated correction batch and one identical rerun.
    
    Every publication stages then atomically no-replace renames and binds the committed specification, clean Git SHA, ordered input hashes, schemas, source/binary hashes, censuses, outputs and test receipts.
    
    Mandatory fail-first tests cover DST/frame mutation, strict-after boundaries, equal-time permutation, LOW/HIGH reflection, double-cost and float-rounding errors, partial-day failures, post-cutoff leakage, incorrect option-shard concatenation and existing-output overwrite.
    
    To prevent another review/fix loop:
    
    - no run begins before the formulation and hashes are frozen;
    - one review produces one correction batch;
    - a second red finding on the same surface returns the work to design instead of starting another patch cycle;
    - no old event-model, pre-cutoff-entry or candidate-row result may be cited as evidence for this experiment.
    
    Assumptions: hindsight MFE exits are accepted solely for certifying entry observability; production exits are deferred. IWM remains the only clock, price and execution authority. RUTW, OI, rates, IV and Greeks are contextual sensors unless a registered interaction earns directional value.
    </proposed_plan>
